QF.id: AIFM CIII AIFs in India and Suitability_4

question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (Category III AIF) has a target corpus of INR 300 crore. The Manager and Sponsor are the same entity. What is the minimum continuing interest the Sponsor/Manager must hold in the fund per SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: INR 7.5 crore, being 2.5% of the corpus
INR 5 crore, being the lower of 5% of corpus or INR 5 crore
INR 10 crore, being the lower of 5% of corpus or INR 10 crore
INR 15 crore, being 5% of the corpus unconditionally

explanation.text: The Logic: Table 4.3 confirms: for Cat III AIFs, Sponsor/Manager must hold at least 5% of corpus OR INR 10 crore, whichever is LOWER. On a INR 300 crore corpus, 5% = INR 15 crore, but the INR 10 crore cap applies since it is the lower of the two. Hence INR 10 crore is the required continuing interest. The Trap: Option A uses Cat I/II's 2.5% sponsor commit. Option B swaps in Cat I/II's INR 5 crore cap. Option D ignores the INR 10 crore absolute cap ('whichever is lower'). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D tests Cat I/II: 2.5% or INR 5 crore, whichever lower. XIX-E tests Cat III: 5% or INR 10 crore, whichever lower. Swapping these values is the single most common trap across the AIF exam family. Manager's Pro-Tip: Structure the sponsor commitment as drawn-down capital called pari-passu with investor capital — not as a subordinated note — to meet SEBI's 'continuing interest' test. On a large-corpus fund (>INR 200 crore), the INR 10 crore hard cap is a massive relief versus Cat I/II's much tighter % commit.
